title: How engagement innovation closes gaps, protects revenue, and strengthens health outcomes
summary: Electronic health records integrations with genetic testing increases operational efficiency, enhances the provider experience and offers precision medicine at scale.
body_markdown:
Health plans face mounting pressure to improve HEDIS®, CMS Star Ratings, quality performance, and protect revenue, all while managing rising operational and budget demands. Yet year after year, gap closure programs continue to underperform, not because of member apathy, but because traditional engagement strategies fail to drive testing completion.


Using the same letters, one-size-fits-all messaging, and single-channel communication strategies every year often fail to meet members where they’re at, especially for older adults, linguistically diverse communities, or those facing social determinants of health barriers. The result is predictable and costly:


- Lower gap closure
- Missed quality performance
- Reduced risk adjustment revenue
- Growing account retention risk


Gaps-in-care programs represent a practical, and potentially lucrative, chance to improve health outcomes and impact reimbursement and revenue because of quality improvement initiatives. Consider:


- Plans experiencing a 1-star increase can see an[8%-12% enrollment boost](https://guidehouse.com/-/media/www/site/insights/healthcare/2018/medicare-advantage-analysis.pdf) the following year
- An increase from 3 to 4 stars can[boost revenue by $12-$16.2 million](https://www.healthleadersmedia.com/strategy/one-star-improvement-can-increase-medicare-advantage-revenue-17) for a 9,600-member health plan
- Medicare Shared Savings Programs[reduced costs by $5.2 billion](https://www.qliqsoft.com/blog/the-financial-upside-of-closing-care-gaps-in-care) , with $3.1 billion of those savings paid to accountable care organizations
- Medicaid managed care organizations may receive financial incentives tied to quality benchmarks, and their contracts in some states require improved quality performance to achieve NCQA accreditation
- Medicare Advantage plans with a 4-star rating or higher can receive up to a 5% quality bonus, representing[approximately $16 billion in additional revenue](https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=eeda99d4-aaaf-4981-acae-be264147e26c)
- Commercial plan designs tied to quality improvement, care coordination, and network optimization can[reduce employer healthcare costs by 10%-30%](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/healthcare/our-insights/reimagining-us-employer-health-benefits-with-innovative-plan-designs)


The good news is recent gaps-in-care pilot programs show something important. Strategic engagement, even small improvements in messaging, channel mix and outreach timing, lead to:


- Lower total cost of care
- More members getting important and needed care
- Measurable increases in member response rates
- Protection of at-risk accounts
- Scalable pathways for sustained gap closure performance
- A better member experience


## Why member engagement innovation matters now


Many health plans struggle to drive participation in[gap closure programs](https://www.labcorp.com/organizations/capabilities/quality-performance/gaps-in-care) for reasons that go beyond lack of member motivation. Common obstacles include transportation challenges, competing responsibilities, uncertainty about outreach legitimacy, low digital engagement, or limited health literacy. Others simply miss or overlook outreach that arrives as long-form mail.


When a plan’s engagement strategy relies on one channel or one message, it almost guarantees that many members won’t see, understand, or act on the reminder. That’s why Labcorp introduced enhancements in pilot programs that aligned channel, message, visual prompts, cadence, and operational support to reflect real-world member behavior.


This combination increased the likelihood that outreach is seen, understood, and acted on, which ultimately strengthens program performance and protects at-risk accounts.


## What the pilots proved: Optimization works


Across multiple pilots, Labcorp introduced a set of engagement innovations tailored to members of health plan populations. Each pilot tested a different mix of messaging, multichannel outreach, and operational enhancements. Pilots aren’t a one size fits all proposition; however, using data and leveraging what works and constantly refining it whether it’s messaging, cadence, channel, or other methods will consistently optimize performance.


While results differed by population and program design, the trend was clear:[better gaps-in-care communication](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/how-labcorp-worked-large-national-plan-improve-member-health) leads to better member engagement. The pilots focused on three core innovations:


**1. Messaging optimization**


Message optimization included:


- Appropriate reading level
- Clear language with tips on what to do
- More supportive visuals
- Strong, simplified calls to action
- Co-branding from trusted organizations


**Why it works:** Members with lower digital engagement or health literacy benefit from concise instructions and visual cues that reduce confusion and friction.


**2. Multichannel outreach**


In addition to better messaging, Labcorp also conducted multichannel outreach, including:


- Optimized pre‑notification letters
- Email reminders
- Postcards
- Text messages
- Reminder letters
- Live calls for select segments


**Why it works:** Repeated touches across different mediums increase the chance the message is noticed. Postcards serve as simple visual nudges; live calls uncover barriers such as transportation, scheduling needs, or confusion about how to access testing and reach members who won't click through email links or navigate digital portals.


**3. Operational pathways that make completion easier**


Finally, operational changes were made involving:


- Scheduling support
- At-home kit options
- [Tracking and reminder capabilities](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/missed-tests-managed-health-how-closing-open-orders-improves-patient-compliance-and-outcomes)
- Optimized outreach cadence to increase responses
- Understanding population needs and tailoring to them


**Why it works:** Once a member decides to act, easy completion pathways prevent drop-off.


Instead of complex technology overhauls, these pilot programs implemented strategic refinements on how, when, and where members received gap closure communications.


## Measurable improvements in member response rates


The pilots demonstrated that modest but thoughtful shifts in engagement strategy can produce meaningful improvements in member action:


- **Pilot 1**


- A major national health insurance plan with a strong concentration in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and surrounding regions
- Targeted a broad portfolio of fully insured commercial, Medicare and Medicaid members supported by a large provider network
- Partnered with behavioral insights experts to develop two pre-notification letters for members, one included a control group and the other incorporated behavioral science-based improvements via simplified language, improved visuals, and better calls to action
- The improvements **increased initial return rates by 2.1% compared** **to the control group** return rates
- **1.8% increase in overall member response rates**


- **Pilot 2**


- A large health insurance plan in New Jersey
- Targeted Medicare Advantage (MA), commercial, and MA dual eligible special needs plan (D-SNP)
- Sent additional email and postcard reminders and live calls for one segment
- Targeted MA emails and postcards **increased response rates by 9%**
- Commercial population emails, postcards, and live calls **improved response rates by 4.7%**
- D-SNP emails and postcards **increased response rates by 3.5%, protecting this at-risk account**


- **Pilot 3**


- A large healthcare organization primarily focused on serving patients over 65 years old in Texas, Florida, and New Mexico
- Sent additional email and postcard reminders to patients
- Primarily senior MA and commercial populations
- **4.3% increase in member response rates**


While these are pilot results, they do show a consistent pattern of how multichannel engagement and message optimization measurably lifts member response rates.


## Multichannel member engagement improves reach across diverse populations


Different members respond to different types of communication. Some prefer email reminders while others, especially older adults or members with limited digital access, respond better to print. Caregivers often depend on postcards as simple visual prompts.


The pilots reinforced:


- Email offers fast, low-cost reinforcement
- Print remains highly effective for digitally underserved members
- Thoughtful cadence and sequencing of channels optimizes cost and return rates
- Postcards provide easy-to-understand reminders for those with low health literacy
- Phone calls help remove access and other barriers and allow questions to be answered in real time
- Clear calls to action and improved health literacy design reduce confusion commonly affecting disadvantaged populations


When layered together, these channels increase reach without adding operational complexity. And most importantly, multichannel outreach doesn’t have to be costly or complex, as Labcorp’s approach focused on strategic touches, not excessive volume.


## Retention, expansion, and partnership value


The commercial impact extended beyond performance metrics. High health plan satisfaction and proven engagement helped:


- Improve health outcomes for members
- Raise anticipated program volume
- Enable program expansion discussions and enhance overall program performance
- Reduce quality performance risk and improve reimbursement revenue
- Support roadmap integration for future core offerings
- Retain important partnerships and continue to advance strategic alignment
- Spread program costs across more members, improving overall health outcomes and plans’ ROI


These improvements by channel and population segment also provide a blueprint for plans to operationalize repeatable playbooks and invest outreach resources where they perform best. This underscores gap closure performance isn't just about CMS Star Ratings or HEDIS compliance, but about demonstrating value and advancing collaborative, strategic relationships.


## Scalable strategies for 2026 and beyond


A key takeaway from the pilots is that improvements in member engagement can be simple, repeatable, and scalable. Refined pilot programs have begun integrating elements such as:


- Enhanced calls to action
- Updated pre‑notification letters
- Postcards as standard outreach components
- Communication templates informed by member behavior
- Multichannel sequencing aligning message cadence with program timelines


These enhancements can be embedded into core gap closure programs without increasing administrative burden for plan partners.


## Why Labcorp’s approach outperforms standard outreach


Labcorp's diagnostic intelligence, powered by more than 45 billion lab results representing approximately 50% of the U.S. population, enables[earlier and more accurate gap identification](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/applying-lab-data-combat-chronic-conditions-strategic-gaps-care-approach) , often before claims data is available. Combined with optimized engagement strategies, this creates a year-round approach that reduces reliance on end-of-year blitzes and distributes completion volume more evenly across calendar periods.


This dual capability allows plans to:


- Identify the right members at the right time
- Reach members via channels they prefer
- Make completion fast and easy
- Optimize program spend and health outcomes
- Capture results with standardized reporting for HEDIS and CMS Star Ratings


And unlike single-modality programs, Labcorp offers both:


- In-person testing across more than 2,200 patient service centers
- At-home kit collection options for convenience and ease of use


This blended model helps expand reach, improve member experience, and streamline operations for plans with limited staff and bandwidth.


## Let’s partner together to close gaps in care


Health plans don’t need massive overhauls to improve quality performance. These pilots show how modest enhancements can significantly improve response rates and help close gaps in care. Which is critical, because small improvements in quality ratings and health outcomes can lead to large financial returns.


Labcorp is committed to being a strategic partner that helps health plans and providers close care gaps year-round. As pilot innovations transition into standard program features, health plans gain access to evidence-based approaches for improving member response without requiring internal resource expansion or technology development.
